conventions.convention: A curve is nonempty, geometrically integral, separated, finite type over its field, and of chain dimension one; smoothness and properness are additional hypotheses.
Local residue is the field trace of the coefficient of t⁻¹dt. The coefficient-field construction requires a finite separable residue extension; perfectness supplies this at every closed point.
The positive principal-parts residue pairing uses a sum of local residues; the fixed normalized Gysin trace is its negative over perfect fields.
Finite potent means some power has finite-dimensional image, allowing exponent zero. Trace linearity is asserted on finite-potent families, not on arbitrary sums of finite-potent endomorphisms.
Divisor degree weights each closed-point coefficient by its residue degree. Geometric-point twists have degree one after algebraic closure; arbitrary closed-point twists need not.
Hyperelliptic over k means a degree-two map to split P¹ over k, with no genus restriction in the definition. Geometric hyperellipticity is tested after algebraic closure.
The different is defined for separable function-field extensions. Its support includes inseparable residue extensions; index e=1 alone does not imply unramifiedness over an imperfect field.
Periodic characters are exp(2πikx), Haar mass is one, and the conjugate multiplier is −i sgn(k), with sgn(0)=0 and constants killed.
The line Hilbert truncation is symmetric at the singularity and uses 1/(πt). It is defined for finite p; the definition supplies neither general principal-value existence nor an L∞ truncation.
Euclidean Fourier transformation uses exp(−2πix·ξ). L² pairings are linear in the first variable; distributional test pairings are bilinear without conjugation.
Riesz transforms are initially L² multiplier operators with symbols −iξ_j/|ξ| and assigned value zero at the null singleton ξ=0; this creates no Euclidean zero-mode exception.
Riesz potentials use unit kernel normalization, Kα(z)=|z|^(α−n) off zero and Kα(0)=0. The potential is assigned a complex value only where its absolute integral is finite.
The strong fractional-integration range is 0<α<n and 1<p<n/α, with 1/q=1/p−α/n. Fourier-analysis choice-bearing arguments assume Countable Choice; the curve suppliers generally assume full Choice.

load_bearing.statement: Assuming AC, a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over any field has the normalized-trace perfect pairing H¹(C,L) × H⁰(C,ωC⊗L⁻¹) → k. Over perfect fields the fixed trace equals the negative principal-parts residue sum.
Assuming AC, every smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field admits a closed immersion into some Pᴺ over that field. The proof uses no Serre duality, Riemann–Roch or residue theory.
Assuming AC, for every divisor D on a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field, l(D)−l(KC−D)=degk(D)+1−g, and i(D)=h¹(C,O(D))=l(KC−D).
Assuming AC, the residues of a rational differential on a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a perfect field have finite support and sum to zero.

Assuming AC, for a commutative k-algebra K acting on V and a k-subspace A with fA<A for every f∈K, there is a unique k-linear residue Ω¹K/k→k with res(f dg)=TrV([f₁,g₁]) for the stated congruent lifts, at least one in E₁.
Assuming AC, H¹(C,L) is canonically the cokernel of Lη→⊕p Lη/Lp for an invertible sheaf on a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field.
Assuming AC, if deg(L)>2g−2 on a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field, then H¹(C,L)=0 and h⁰(C,L)=deg(L)+1−g.

Assuming Countable Choice, C extends uniquely and consistently to bounded complex-linear operators on periodic Lp for every 1<p<∞, kills constants, and has no bounded compatible strong L¹ or L∞ extension.

Assuming Countable Choice, for every Schwartz f the symmetric Hilbert principal value exists at every point, equals convolution with pv(1/(πx)), and has Fourier transform −i sgn(ξ) times the Fourier transform of f.
Assuming Countable Choice, S(T)=∫₀ᵀ sin(u)/u du tends to π/2, satisfies |S(T)|≤3 and |S(T)|≤T for T≤1, and its tails satisfy |∫ᴮA sin(u)/u du|≤2/A for 1≤A<B.
Assuming Countable Choice, for 0<α<n and 1<p<n/α, NR(x)≤C Rα Mf(x) when Mf(x)<∞, while FR(x)≤C R^(α−n/p)‖f‖p at every x. The integrals and convergent potential are representative-independent.
Assuming Countable Choice, for θ=αp/n∈(0,1) and Mf(x)<∞, the Riesz integral converges absolutely and |Iαf(x)|≤C(Mf(x))^(1−θ)‖f‖p^θ, including the explicitly handled zero cases.

concerns.concern: Fact F9 says u=log(e/r) maps (0,e⁻¹) onto (1,∞); its actual image is (2,∞). Steps 1.2, 1.4 and 2.1 consequently use false equalities with lower limit 1, and step 3.1 omits −log 2 from the annular integral. For s=2 the actual radial integral is 1/2, whereas the printed transformed integral is 1. The membership, origin divergence and essential-unboundedness conclusions remain true, but the computations as written do not.

Fact F1 asserts representative independence for a local principal part multiplied by 'a rational section' of the dual canonical twist. The opened definition requires a regular stalk section. On P¹ at t=0 with L=O and s=t⁻¹dt, representatives 0 and 1 of the zero principal part give residues 0 and 1. The actual theorem uses a global regular s and remains supported; F1 is an overstrong citation. The A-page prose also describes this pairing using rational dual sections without the regularity qualification.

Clause 3 says that for general critical Lp inputs, subtracting the far-kernel term 'changes it by a constant'; external_dependency.exact_statement likewise assigns the finite-constant equality and same-BMO-class comparison to general f. The opened Harboure text restricts that comparison to compactly supported f, then separately defines the renormalized extension for general f (printed pp. 7–8). For f(y)=|y|⁻α/log|y| on |y|>e, f∈L^(n/α) but the far constant and raw positive potential diverge. Source: [Harboure, Spaces of smooth functions](https://congreso.us.es/cidama/activos/cursos/EHarbourefull.pdf).

Fact F3 calls the complete linear system '|L| ... of dimension h⁰(C,L)=r+1'. The opened suppliers distinguish the section-space dimension r+1 from projective-system dimension r. Here h⁰(L)=3 and |L| has dimension 2. The theorem and proof use the correct P² target, but this cited fact is false as written.

Step 2.1 applies the mean value theorem to the interval with endpoints A=|x−h| and B=|x| without treating A=B. That case is allowed, including h=0. The radial difference is then zero and the remaining coordinate difference satisfies the bound directly.

Step 5.1 infers ∫qψR≥∫[4,R−2]q from ψR≥0 and ψR=1 on the latter interval. Its support can meet (0,1/2), where q<0. An additional argument controlling or cancelling that fixed negative contribution is needed; the logarithmic divergence conclusion survives such a bound.

Step 1.2 describes the completed regular expansion of s as 'the second finite as a section of the stalk κ(p)[[t]] dt'. Such a power-series expansion need not be finite. Only finitely many coefficients contribute to the displayed residue, which is what the subsequent argument uses.
Between steps 2.2 and 3.1 there are unnumbered paragraphs labelled (ii)–(iv) that repeat the corresponding clauses of step 3.1. They add no mathematical content and obscure the proof numbering.

seams_checked.note: The main DVR, divisor, canonical-bundle, finite-map and separable-different uses preserve the opened supplier hypotheses. One exception is cor-degree-three-line-bundle-embeds-genus-one-plane-cubic F3: it converts the supplier's r+1-dimensional section space into an r+1-dimensional complete linear system, losing projectivization. The reverse page prose defers duality appropriately. The batch-8 page-edge ledger still says this supplier page is missing, although its file is present and was read; the owning writer must reconcile that stale row.

The consumers quote l(D)−i(D)=degk(D)+1−g for arbitrary fields, geometrically integral smooth proper curves, signed divisors and AC. They obtain i(D)=l(KC−D) from separate duality, rather than attributing it to Euler-characteristic Riemann–Roch. Degree-zero and negative-degree uses retain their hypotheses. The reverse page prose explicitly defers the sharp canonical-degree and degree-threshold claims to duality. Its batch-8 page-edge ledger also still says the supplier page is missing despite the current file.
